subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Systemic Risk and Too Big to Fail
description: A micro-lesson that makes Systemic Risk and Too Big to Fail usable.

hook.text: A bank is so large that its failure would collapse the financial system. The government must save it. That's bad.

buildup.text: Systemic risk is the danger that one institution's failure triggers a chain reaction across the entire financial system.

discovery.text: After 2008, regulators designated 30 global banks as 'systemically important' with extra capital and oversight.

twist.text: Too big to fail creates moral hazard. Banks know they'll be rescued, so they take bigger risks.

climax.text: Regulators try to end too big to fail. But systemically important banks keep getting bigger.

punchline.text: Too big to fail. Too big to punish. Still getting bigger.

quiz.question: What problem does 'too big to fail' create?
options: Moral hazard — banks take bigger risks knowing they'll be rescued
Governments earn profits from bank rescues
